decisions.reason: As a core bread line that builds directly on our established baking strengths and was given its own page, we would continue it because the investment and visible commitment are meaningful and there is no clear sign of failure.

We would keep the premium raisin Christmas stollen because it fits our traditional confectionery business, has been publicly highlighted, and its gold medal is a strong positive signal that reinforces prior commitment.

We would continue the rye mixed bread with seeds because it is close to our core assortment, uses existing know-how and facilities, and our public introduction makes withdrawal harder without clear negative evidence.

We would keep the dark barley malt rye bread since it extends our established bread range with limited strategic risk and there is no result suggesting that the original launch commitment should be reversed.

We would retain the marzipan Christmas stollen because it is closely aligned with our seasonal specialty business and the prior public launch supports staying the course absent clear disappointing outcomes.

We would keep the ancient grain bread because it was launched as a showcased new Meisterstück, is still rooted in our bread craftsmanship, and management would be inclined to justify that visible commitment rather than withdraw early.
